source_evidence: Your investing timeframe, also called your time horizon, is the number of months, years, or decades you plan to invest to achieve your financial goal.
answer: Your investment time horizon is how long you plan to invest toward a financial goal. It matters when considering asset allocation: investors with longer time horizons may feel comfortable with riskier or more volatile investments, while those with shorter time horizons may prefer less risky or less volatile investments. These are general tendencies, not a one-size-fits-all allocation; the source also notes that allocation depends on personal risk tolerance.
